Systematic Review Details Enterprise Resource Planning Systems Transitioning Toward Artificial Intelligence

Artificial intelligence is transforming enterprise resource planning platforms from transactional backbones into intelligent, data-centric systems designed for automation, prediction, process monitoring, and decision support, according to a systematic review published in the Journal of Big Data. Researchers conducted an evidence synthesis to evaluate how machine learning and analytics intersect with operational enterprise workflows, mapping research patterns that have emerged across the operational software domain over the past decade.

The investigation addressed a persistent fragmentation within enterprise software literature, where research streams have historically split across technical development, organizational implementation, and specialized analytical applications. Current literature has infrequently differentiated between artificial intelligence capabilities directly embedded within standard workflow architectures and external analytics layers developed on top of enterprise data repositories. To clarify these operational distinctions, the authors conducted a structured examination across ten years of peer-reviewed literature.

Using a structured coding protocol guided by PRISMA guidelines, the authors analyzed 80 Scopus-indexed publications published between 2014 and 2024. The systematic review coupled qualitative synthesis with bibliometric performance analysis and science mapping.

The bibliometric network analysis revealed that enterprise resource planning represented the most central keyword within the analyzed literature, recording 13 occurrences and a total link strength of 42. Following this primary anchor, data analytics and information management emerged as the next most prominent conceptual nodes, with each term recording six occurrences and a total link strength of 23.

Analysis of document formats demonstrated a balanced distribution between technical presentation and archival journal scholarship across the sample. Conference papers accounted for 47.5 percent of the analyzed documents, while journal articles represented 42.5 percent of the total sample. The authors noted that this publication pattern reflects a rapidly expanding academic domain that continues to develop simultaneously through technical conference proceedings and peer-reviewed journal outlets.

Science mapping of geographic contributions indicated that international collaboration remains limited within artificial intelligence and enterprise system scholarship. Research influence and publication volume remain concentrated around a relatively small set of academic contributors rather than being distributed across extensive cross-border institutional networks.

The systematic coding process identified five primary thematic domains structuring current scholarship: artificial intelligence and machine learning in enterprise resource planning, integrated decision support and business analytics, business-process optimization, predictive and prescriptive analytics, and business intelligence inside operational platforms. Across these categories, literature demonstrated the strongest conceptual maturity in operational forecasting, process automation, and managerial decision support frameworks.

Despite strong theoretical interest in advanced analytics, the synthesis highlighted significant gaps in practical enterprise deployment. The literature remains noticeably weaker regarding deployment-level validation, architectures tailored specifically for small and medium-sized enterprises, algorithmic explainability, and scalable integration protocols for legacy enterprise systems. The authors concluded by proposing a structured research agenda to advance intelligent enterprise systems from isolated prototypes toward explainable, interoperable analytics ecosystems.

Subject of Research: Systematic review and bibliometric analysis of artificial intelligence integration in enterprise resource planning systems

Article Title: AI-enhanced ERP systems: a systematic review and bibliometric analysis of intelligent enterprise analytics

Article References: Abdelwahid, I. M., Haroun, R., Iktish, S. A., Al Bayaa, L., & Bahroun, Z. (2026). AI-enhanced ERP systems: a systematic review and bibliometric analysis of intelligent enterprise analytics. Journal of Big Data. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40537-026-01592-5
